newsitem.title: USA: BRENT CRUDE REGAINS GROUND IN LATE U.S. TRADING.
newsitem.headline: BRENT CRUDE REGAINS GROUND IN LATE U.S. TRADING.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude oil retraced some its earlier losses in late U.S. paper trading on Wednesday, traders said.
A pair of full boats of September Brent switched hands at $19.25 a barrel, up seven cents from the IPE close in London.
Two partial cargoes traded at $19.20 and $19.21 a barrel in exchange-for-physical transactions for a total of 300 lots, traders said.
After the window closed, another partial cargo of 50 lots traded at $19.21.
September Brent was last pegged at $19.24-26.
Intermonth activity was limited, with a September/October spread trading at minus nine cents a barrel, steady with earlier deals.
